{{short description|Method in linear algebra}}
In [[linear algebra]], an '''orthogonal diagonalization''' of a [[normal matrix]] (e.g. a [[symmetric matrix]]) is a [[diagonalizable matrix|diagonalization]] by means of an [[orthogonal matrix|orthogonal]] change of coordinates.<ref name="Poole 2010 p. 411">{{cite book | last=Poole | first=D. | title=Linear Algebra: A Modern Introduction | publisher=Cengage Learning | year=2010 | isbn=978-0-538-73545-2 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FByELohRQd8C&pg=PA411 | access-date=12 November 2018 | page=411}}</ref>

The following is an orthogonal diagonalization algorithm that diagonalizes a [[quadratic form]] ''q''(''x'') on '''R'''<sup>''n''</sup> by means of an orthogonal change of coordinates ''X''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''PY''.<ref>[[Seymour Lipschutz]] ''3000 Solved Problems in Linear Algebra''.</ref>
* Step 1: Find the symmetric matrix ''A'' that represents ''q'' and find its [[characteristic polynomial]] Δ({{itco|''t''}}).
* Step 2: Find the [[eigenvalue]]s of ''A'', which are the [[root of a polynomial|roots]] of Δ({{itco|''t''}}).
* Step 3: For each eigenvalue ''λ'' of ''A'' from step 2, find an [[orthogonal basis]] of its [[eigenspace]].
* Step 4: Normalize all eigenvectors in step 3, which then form an [[orthonormal basis]] of '''R'''<sup>''n''</sup>.
* Step 5: Let ''P'' be the [[matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] whose columns are the normalized [[eigenvector]]s in step 4.
Then {{nowrap|1=''X'' = ''PY''}} is the required orthogonal change of coordinates, and the diagonal entries of ''P''<sup>T</sup>''A''{{px2}}''P'' will be the eigenvalues ''λ''<sub>1</sub>, ..., ''λ''<sub>''n''</sub> that correspond to the columns of ''P''.

Such decomposition exists by the [[Spectral Theorem#Normal_matrices|spectral theorem]].
